title: John Simpson Joins The Lounge | Baltimore Ravens
text: Welcome into the lounge. I'm Ryan Mink joined by Garrett Downing and we are thrilled to sit down with John Simpson. We we continue on the reunion tour with Glas Campbell as our last guest and now John thanks for joining us. New new digs. John came in here. He was like, "Wow, you all upgraded since last >> here now." >> 23. So John, just you know what made the Ravens the fit for you to come back? Um, honestly, like just the the from the last time I was here, um, it just felt like home. Um, and >> I just felt like me getting that opportunity to come back, it was like a no-brainer. Um, and just >> being around the guys and and just being in this environment, just it just I feel like I I belong here. So, >> awesome. So, as you went through the free agency process, you know, you were somebody the Ravens clearly went into this offseason saying, "We want to improve the offensive line." and you were a guy that they targeted in that process. Take us through the conversations that you had with the Ravens during free agency that ultimately led to you coming back here. >> Yeah. Um their their main thing was just like just bringing that that um tenacity back. Um I guess you can call it and and just and just like being physical and just trying to be a dominant force. Um and and that's that's basically all they were telling me. um everything that they wanted me to bring to the table. And I was just like, "Hey, look, I get I'm gonna do everything I can for y'all, man." Because like I said, like this is like home. And it's like the guys that are in this building is like they're all like my brother. So it's like I got to go crazy for these for these dudes. So like I think the reason they brought me here is the reason like I feel like I belong in a sense. Do >> do you feel like there's a special connection? You're kind of speaking to this and I'm curious like do you feel like there's a special connection that you have with the Ravens organization? I remember when you were here the first time, you talked about coming here and when you when you signed here, coming from the Raiders, feeling like you didn't really have confidence at that point and you came here >> and then you you blossomed, you ended up becoming a starter, you played at a high level, you get the big contract and like all those things kind of converged here and happened here >> for sure. >> Uh does that was that whole story part of the reason that you felt like you wanted to come back here? >> I think so. I I I think just like being here for that one year. Um it kind of like you said gave me that confidence that I needed. Um and like beyond just like the player, it's like deeper than that here. Um they kind of like treat you like legit family and like you walking in the hallway and they might be a janitor. He knows your name. I know the janitor's name. You know what I'm saying? So it's like >> that type of relationship and everybody just treats you so well here and it's just like why wouldn't you want to be a part of something like this? >> Cool. What did that 2023 season do for you as a player and as a person? >> I think it it kind of like showed me like like how it's supposed to be done, I guess you can say. >> Um because there's a lot of there's a lot of guys that that were that was in that old line room. Like you had guys like Kevin Zitler, right? >> Morgan Moses, you got Ronnie, you got guys like that >> and you just see it. You come in, you see like those guys working like you know what I'm saying? It's like, okay, I can I can do that. I can I can fit in with these guys and I can I can do exactly what they're doing. And I think it's just that part gave me that like that juice. >> Yeah. And and Garrett brought it up, you know, the confidence aspect. That was such a cool part of your story that season was seeing you, >> you know, it's cool to see like a player be a so transparent about it and open about like their feelings and their emotions and all that. And then like to see you grow and really take off that year. Can you talk about what it's like going from that three years ago to now being a prized free agent, right, that like people are going after, you know? >> Right. No, I mean it it definitely is a it was a long like process obviously to get me where I am today. >> Yeah. >> Um but I mean it was it I know it was a it was a >> I don't even know how to put it. It was just like a >> kind of like a light like a light switch almost like I just needed >> that. I don't know. I don't even know how to put it. But I just I feel like the confidence that I got like being here and just like in like going through like a winning, you know what I'm saying? Organization. It just kind of helped me. It >> like I said, it showed me what what how it's supposed to be done >> and you get momentum. You kind of And then I remember like when when you were named the starter near the end of training camp and it felt like, you know, you've been putting you've been stacking days in training camp and all that stuff and then you're named the start and it was like, "All right, off we go." Right. And then once you build the momentum then your career that's how careers happen. >> Exactly. Exactly. And it just you know like every every I feel like every situation cuz like the my the way my whole career started it >> it wasn't like ideal. Um and you know everything happens for a reason and I like I can't I kind of like was looking back on I was like >> in the moment I was like >> uh what's the word? What do people always say? Uh down on myself I guess you could say. M >> and I was just like, man, like when I got here, kind of like, like I said, it just was like, no need to be down on yourself. Just work. If you work, >> it'll pay it'll all pay off. And and ever since then, I just never really looked back. And I just was like, I'm going to put my best foot forward every day. And just whatever happens happens. Um, and just control what I can control. Yeah. >> And I feel like once I started thinking like that, it kind of like everything just like kind of flipped >> cuz I was trying to trying so hard to control >> like obviously things that I couldn't control like what the coaches think of me or what I like. But I'm like at the end of the day just go be yourself. Just play ball, have fun >> and you know just made it made the the sport >> made me fall back in love with the sport again. So >> yeah. Yeah. Well and and then it paid dividends. So you play at a high level and so you you go from that point and then you get the contract with with the Jets. and you know, you were at that point a couple years ago, you were the big free agent acquisition for them um as they were looking to to improve their roster. What did it mean for you to get that contract extension from them? And what did you learn and take away from the two years that you spent in New York? >> Um it was huge, man. I I I met a lot of great people uh at the Jets. The the O line like group was like some of the best people I ever met in my life. Um like they're brothers forever. Um, it was just like having the opportunity to go and like get out there and like play at a different at a different organization was just it was huge because >> like I said like going into that year that I was here, I didn't really have that confidence and I didn't know what that what the year after that was going to hold. I had no idea. Um, but I mean it was like they gave me the opportunity. I just kind of like ran with it. So it was cool. How is 2026 John Simpson different from 2023 John Simpson as a person and how have you improved as a player? >> Um well 2023 I didn't have any kids. >> Got two kids now. >> That'll change. That'll change. >> Uh um besid I mean besides that um I try to be I try to be as I try to be the same person every day. So as far as like personality like like I'm the same person, >> right? I already got that. >> I like 23. I wouldn't I wouldn't say much on the field. I wasn't really like a talker. I didn't talk much. But now I'm like I'm I talk I talk a lot of trash. >> You kind of come into your a little bit. You feel yourself. You know what you're capable of. >> Yeah. Yeah. I get into it a little bit. I get I get rowdy sometimes out there. So >> that's funny is like I would not imagine that because like you sit down, you're like one of the nicest guys. like you're one of my favorite guys to talk to just because you have this like great, you know, gregarious personality, but like on the field you get a little bit nasty. >> Different beast, man. Different. You got to be out there cuz it's like they trying to they trying to they trying to take your head off. So, it's like, hey, it's either me or you, buddy. So, that's kind of how I look at it. >> Well, you mentioned the tenacity aspect, and I think that that probably speaks to it. And like it's kind of a mindset like playing with an edge and a mindset and just this mentality that like I'm going to no one's going to run me over like I'm going to be that guy. >> Yeah. Oh yeah. >> And so coming here you have some veteran presence on the offensive line of course with with Ronnie next to you. >> But what is how do you try to bring that and instill that uh to to this group as a whole? >> I would say just being like a leader like by example. Um, and and like I've been saying this whole time, just coming in and just like put my best foot forward and then those guys that are next to me or behind me or whatever, they'll like hopefully follow follow that lead and obviously lead >> in the right way and not necessarily just always like spazzing or crashing out, whatever people call it nowadays. >> He's got kids. You already know where the kid lingo, >> right? So like like like beyond that just like being a being a guy that not only that I can like can show them what to do but a guy that those guys can come and talk to and if they have any like issues or anything like that like yo like I've been in the league for seven years. I got cut. I didn't been on practice squad. I've been you know what I'm saying? I've been around the league for a little bit. So just somebody that they that they can come and talk to and just >> be there for him. For sure. >> Who talked to you about the the desire to reestablish the tenacity? Was that Eric Dcasta when you were he was courting you? Was that when you got here with Jesse Mentor? >> It it was uh Coach Le. Coach Le his his biggest thing is uh speed off the ball and and he like obviously he watched my film and stuff like that and he he loves like how I how I move and stuff. So he was like just bring that and just be like be who you are. Just be nasty. Be like bring that tenacity >> and everything else will like speak for itself. >> So speed off the ball is like your first step. How quick you are off the snap. >> Yeah. Just get off the ball. Speed off the ball. That's his big thing. Every after we break a meeting and he's speed off the ball. Let's go. We got speed off the ball. Literally. Literally. So, >> okay. All right. So, we're going to actually have Coach Leford on as a guest, our next guest. So, >> that's the first thing you got to say to us. >> Speed off the ball. That'll be the first question. Tell us about him. What What's he like, you know, other than speed off the ball? What is he kind of stressing to you guys? >> Uh, speed off the ball. No, he he man he's like I think I think so far like he's one of like the best uh teachers I think I've ever had. Like beyond like beyond being a coach like he's a great teacher and um and he wants he wants it to be to a point where it's just like you you get the play call, you get up there, you get to the line fast and you just run it. Like he don't want you second guessing or anything like that. Um, so he kind of like tries to simplify it and try to make everything as un like >> easy to understand as possible. >> Um, so I mean I love I love the way he coaches and I love that like he he's going to get the best out of each each and every one of his players >> and he doesn't have to do a whole lot of cussing and hoot and hollering. >> He's going to be he's going to love you like he's like you're one of his kids and you know what I'm saying? And that's that's everything I got so far. his only otaas, but >> um he's like I said, one of the the better teachers I've ever had. >> Yeah, it's cool. That's cool. Well, you talked about being a leader to some of the young guys. Of course, one of the young guys is the rookie first round pick Yane. Uh having him come in and join this group. Uh what are your impressions of him and and any conversations you guys have been able to have so far? >> Yeah. Uh so I haven't really been able to talk to him much, but uh we've been in the weight room today. Strong strong dude, man. Yeah. >> Um and I've I watched some of his film and stuff like that. I'm probably a little nerd, but >> yeah, >> but he's a he's a he's a dog and he's I think he's he got what it takes to to play at this level. You know what I'm saying? And compete against some of the best in this league. So, it's going to be it's going to be fun to watch. >> Like to I just keep coming back to this point about tenacity and like mindset on the offensive line. I'm like to me you two guys at guard like that's exactly what we're talking about. Like like everything that I've seen from him at the college level of being like just a bulldozer, tough mindset leader. Same things for you. How excited are you for the the two of you guys as as kind of lynchpin pieces all along this offensive line to help really kind of instill that mentality on this team? >> It's going to be it's going to be great, man. It's going to be fun. And and I think having having two like interior guys or how many ever? Three, I guess you say, you know, we know two right now. But >> um just having having those guys, I feel like that's kind of where it all starts. um obviously in the interior because it we're the first people to make contact. You know what I'm saying? Center snaps the ball, >> guards and centers, we we getting hit first. >> So it's like you got to kind of have that that nastiness to you because every every time the ball snaps is it's like a it's like a car wreck. >> So it's like just keep going like just keep stacking, keep going, keep going. And I think it's going to be huge because this like you said like this team like we need that and I think that'll help get us over the hump for sure. Yeah, I'm interested in that because, you know, there's the conversation about positional value and it's always been tackles, tackles, tackles, left tackle, right? That's always like been the spot, but it seems like guard and center are now kind of catching up to the tackles. >> And and do why do you think that is? And to your point of like we're making contact first, do you feel like guards kind of establish a team's identity in the trenches? >> I would say I would say a little bit. Um, it definitely it all starts in the trenches. Um, and guard, tackle, center, no matter what, you like I feel like you got to be a dog if you going to play on the O line or D line. >> Um, so I feel like hey, like if you out there, you got to be a dog. And I feel like if you if you I mean I don't know, you just can't go out there half stepping. If you you know what I'm saying, that tenacity, it is what it is. You gota either you got it or you don't. Yeah. Um, and some people just need to be some people just need to be woken up a little bit. Like me, I was had to go woken up a little bit. >> Wake up a little bit. You know what I'm saying? >> Unleash the dog. >> Sure. Exactly. >> I'm also curious about, you know, one of the conversations has been left, right, you know, left guard, right guard between you and Wangga. He played left guard in college. You obviously been playing left guard. you know, what's your viewpoint on that and how that might shake out and is it harder for a veteran to maybe switch if one of them's going to switch? >> Yeah, I mean, I would say I would definitely say it's harder for a vet to switch. Uh, but like >> it's honestly whatever whatever they need me to like whatever they need me to do. Um, I've only played left guard. >> Um, I play a little bit of right guard, preseason games and stuff like that. >> The past three years it's been exclusively left. >> Left guard. Yeah. But, I mean, like I said, I'm I'm here to help the team win, man. I I I just want to play and and >> get to that that big stage. >> Yeah, >> that's that's cool. >> So, I I mentioned this in terms of a priority for the team this offseason being just improving the offensive line. Like that's that's clear that the Ravens, they've talked about it many times, Eric Casa, Jesse Mentor, like they want to improve in the trenches. How good do you feel about the group that's currently in place here? >> Hey, listen. We got some we got some dogs. cuz we got some boys that's going that's working right now and like like it's it's crazy it's going to be it's going to be a good one y'all. Like >> if anything happened to one person up there on the on the starting five, next guy coming in, he going to be he going to be ready >> and like and that's a that's a testament to like our strength staff, but also like I said, coach Le and like how he's teaching and stuff like that. I feel like it's all going to go hand in hand and it's going to be this O line group is this year going to be it's going to be fun to watch. >> I I like hear that. Definitely like hear that. I mean, that's that's what you need. That's where it starts identity wise, like offense. You need to be able This is a team that like wants to run the ball, of course, with Derrick Henry in the back field and establish that identity. The a question on the O line is is center, of course, just like you don't know who it's going to be at this point. Um, but you have two good guards next to the center that whoever's in there'll have, you know, you two guys to help uh surround him and elevate uh him. So, what's your view of the center position and and the guys that you have in that mix and and how that ultimately shakes out? >> Yeah, I mean, we got some talented guys. Um, you got Cory Bulock, you got uh Danny P, uh, you got Javon, uh, Gwyn. Look, those boys are, like I said, they competing. They competing their asses off right now. And they just like like I said, wait room out there running. We could be doing some, uh, we could be doing karaokeis. We trying to we trying to get to the 10 yard line, the fast, who trying to get there fast. You know what I'm saying? Like everything's a competition now. And that's like that's what drives I feel like drives you to be better. >> Um, and that's kind of like what that was my mentality when I first got here. said I I was like come in there just do everything 100% just go hard and then everything will like these guys will follow you and I'm not really like a I'm a fun goofy like dancing around type of guy I'm not going to yell at you like if either you going to work or you ain't like this is your job and so um if I I feel like if I come in with that mentality of if I'm going to work these guys you know what I'm saying they'll they'll they'll fall in >> is is there a little bit of a feeling after Tyler Linderbalm left in free agency with with his loss that like all right it is a little bit more on me and the guards to kind of help make sure that the interior of the O line is it remains strong. >> Uh I wouldn't say that I I would I don't like putting pressure on myself. I'm like either either >> I mean I just got to do my job at the end of the day. Um and and you know the center got to do his job. So >> like I said, this is our job. >> Yeah, that's fair. So, so, um, I I I wouldn't I wouldn't I don't I don't put too much pressure on myself as far as that goes, but >> I just want to be the best leader that I can be. >> That's fair. >> How excited are you to be blocking for Derrick Henry? >> I say, listen, >> listen, every day, every day I come here, I'm like, yo, I'm going to tell my kid, my kids, and my grandkids, like, I block for Derek, Lamar, you know what I'm saying? That's crazy. Like, that's insane. Like, who who else can really I mean, a few people, but like that's that's just insane. So that's going to be that's going to be something something to to to talk about for sure in the future. >> So you were here in 23, you know, as we mentioned and you know that team went to the AFC Championship >> and for you being at you were on you were knocking on the door with that group. >> How much does that drive you being so close and coming back here? Do you feel like it's unfinished business? Like how do you view that? >> Yeah, most definitely. Uh that was the first thing I put on Twitter when I when I uh got the call like unfinished business. I was like, look, like it's it's like >> I don't know. Like you said, I've I've been in this league. This will be my seventh year. That's the closest I've ever I've ever gotten. And it's like I kind of know from that from that year, I kind of know I know what it looks like and I know what it looks like to get to that point, but we just got to get over that hump. >> And I feel like that's the next step here. Um and I think it'll be cool to see all that transpire. >> Yeah. Well, you're going to be a big part of getting us over that hump, John. Thank you so much, man. Really appreciate it. Appreciate y'all. >> Welcome back into the lounge. We are coming to you from the SeatGeek studio. Thanks to John Simpson for stopping by. It's good to have him back in the building. Uh just a guy that is is I really like him. Uh he's a fun guy to talk to and has a great personality and like we talked with him like he change he's he falls into that category of like the switch flips when he gets on the field. He plays with an edge and I really think that that is something that the Ravens were looking for on this offensive line. like they want good play of course, but you also want a mindset like you need you you're the group that's going to establish the identity of the offense and John is somebody who can help in that regard and Van Go will as well. But I just think that having a veteran presence there that you can put in that's going to be your clear-cut starter that that works hard that plays with edge. I just think that's going to be a really good thing for this group. >> Yeah, obviously that was kind of a missing ingredient to last year's team. the Ravens wanted to get better and and more physical and kind of reestablish themselves on the interior line. And John Simpson is a guy that will absolutely do that. You know, he mentioned his career arc. He was a early early round pick out of Clemson uh by the the Las Vegas Raiders and then just kind of didn't pan out there. Ended up getting benched and then getting released by them. The Ravens ended up picking them up late in the 2022 season. >> Real late. >> Real very late. league in December. >> And kind of stashed him to a degree uh with the the expectation or belief that he could compete in 2023 for the job. He won the starting job in 23 coming out of training camp and then just off and running from there. So, it's just cool to see a player. It you know what it reminded me of a little bit while he was talking was Kyle Vanoi, you know, who who was a draft pick that didn't pan out for the Detroit Lions got cut and has now had a great career. And like John Simpson is a guy who uh is still relatively early in his career when you look at snaps and stuff like that because he kind of got a later start. He he's fresher. >> Uh it's a good young I think still ascending player who plays the way the Ravens want to play. >> I just think that when you look at the offensive line this year, first of all, the Ravens wanted to improve it. Then you add in the fact that they lost Tyler Linderbomb in free agency. So it's like one of your best pieces is now is now gone. So, what do you do with that offensive line? Well, you wanted to improve the guard play. You go get one of the top guards that's on the market who you just know again you can put him into the starting lineup. He's going to play at a high level. He's going to give you everything he's got. And like that's a good starting point there. And now you add Venga on the other side to go along with two tackles who are in place and Ronnie and Roger. And I just feel like look, there's still a question at center. We don't know who the starting center is going to be as as we talked about with him. But I I think that with the other four pieces in place, I feel really good about this offensive line going into the season. I I think that it's going to I think it's going to be a good unit and I think it's going to be improved. >> Mhm. >> And so like where were the holes on where are the holes on this team? That was one that existed last year and I think the Ravens have really addressed it. Again, not diminishing that you got to find your center. You got to figure that piece out. But I think that the line overall with John and Yane is going to be in a really good spot. >> It reminds me of some of the the 2018, 2019, 2020 offensive lines, you know, that had Matt Skur in the center of an undrafted center right in the middle. And then you had Marshall Yard spot, you know, you had Ben Powers and and some other guys going back to the other left guard spot. that was always kind of a new guy plugged in there every several years, but had some high level guard play there at left on the left side, too. And then Ronnie Stanley, you know, at left tackle. So, >> center Bradley Boseman is another one who played guard and center here, but he was a late round pick. He was a sixth round pick. So Scura late undrafted, Bradley Boseman late round pick >> like and so those guys worked in at center there and it worked and they and the line play some of the I mean 2019 that line was insane. Now Marshall was >> really the anchor of that group, him and Ronnie, but that that line was as good as any I've seen here. >> Yeah, exactly. So I I think that this line can be very good. John clearly believes this is going to be a very strong offensive line. And and let's also not forget one one other point about John is the past two years he's been playing in a Jets offense that was really not a very good offense. Not because of how he was playing, but >> they were just they had multiple problems, right? Put John Simpson in the the kind of prime of his career back in a Ravens offense with Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry in the back field and let's see what he becomes. Also, >> yeah, I think he's just going to I think this I continue to feel like this offense is just going to hit the ground running this year. They're going to be able to I think at times last year an area where the Ravens struggled offensively was being able to run the ball when they had to run the ball like and just designed run plays. You you need four yards like go out there and do it. And I think they're going to be able to do that. I'm not going to say with ease goal line situations like short yardage situations. Like those are spots where you just need to win the yard. You would need to win the line of scrimmage and get a yard. And with the pieces that the Ravens have now, I think that they're going to be really good in those types of situations. >> I mean, remember all the tush pushes, the the trouble getting in on tush pushes, two of them on on the goal line. I don't think that now you got John Simpson and Wena in the middle pushing that pile. >> All right. >> I feel good about a lot better. Exactly. And that's kind of to the tenacity, the physicality, all that, and the fast first step. >> Yeah, exactly. Well, we're going to have to ask Coach Leford about that. We have him on this week. So, uh, stay tuned for that. As always, you can email us at the lounge at ravens.n.net. One other program we note I want to mention, of course, the NFL schedule comes out Thursday night. We are all excited to see what that schedule's going to look like. Of course, our travel draft, most importantly, that's going to be part of the schedule. >> Stacking the board right now. >> Yeah, exactly. We're working that. I know Brazil probably pretty high on your list. Uh, >> I'm not going to tip my hand. >> So, uh, we're going to wait and see, uh, how that comes out. But Thursday night, uh, 8:00 is when the schedule drops. And so, we are going to be ready for that. Have a podcast breaking that all down for you, uh, Thursday night. So, uh, send us your emails, your thoughts. Uh, you can again email us the lounge ravens.n.net. Thank you so much for watching and listening. We'll be back with you again later this week.

title: Ryan Fitzpatrick: "I'm So Excited For The New Stadium, So Excited To See Everyone" | One Bills Live
text: Thursday Night Football season opener week two new Highark Stadium Bills Lions go. I found out now that I'm on the other side of this on the TV side a few hours before you guys did it. >> Okay. And so I was sitting on a secret and I couldn't tell anybody. I was so excited and this was the game that I wanted and we did it. I will see you week two. I'm so excited. So excited for the new stadium. So excited to see everybody and obviously treat to watch Josh Allen play football. >> Being in the new stadium fits. I think about Amazon. I think about the show that you guys do and you guys are so good at being passionate about the game and I think a lot of fans relate to you all because fans are so passionate about the NFL and I can't think of a better crew to be at the home opener for the new Highark Stadium than you guys because I feel like you're going to do a perfect job like encapsulating all of that passion and really showing the world what this new stadium is like. How excited are you to be on a stage to do something like that? >> Well, we we feel very privileged to be able to have this responsibility and we do view it as a responsibility uh because we were chosen to present this game and to introduce the world to this stadium. And so, um you know, we'll go onsite. I'm sure our producers are heading out there pretty soon just to be able to make this as special as possible and to check out all the great places and where we're going to have a setup and you know there are certain shows that we call it go big that we'll go big for. We'll probably set something up outside. It'll be an amazing scene out there. Um and and we just feel very lucky and fortunate to be able to present this game to everybody. You had the opportunity to kind of go through the stadium once before back in the fall when you were here for a Thursday night game. Obviously, a lot more finishing touches have been put on it since then, but what do you recall about that that has you kind of looking forward to an actual game now? >> Well, I didn't know when I walked through it that it was going to be grass. So, now I know that and I've been telling everybody that. That was new for me. but less seats, more intimate, but it's going to be louder. Um, they found a way to do that. I thought the sightelines from every seat in there uh was very excited. You know what, Chris? I ended up buying season tickets. Why? I don't know. Wow. >> Because I got caught up in the hype >> and I bought four season tickets. How many times I'm going to be able to go? I the one time I'm gonna be able to go, I'm gonna be busy working the game, but I figured I've got enough friends, family, teachers, first responders, whoever it is. Um, I have four tickets. >> You got old neighborhood friends still here, right? >> We'll share as well. >> Well, they're going to now. I shouldn't have told you that. They're going to be hitting me up now texting. >> Yeah, you probably shouldn't cuz the jig is up now. I mean, heck, you don't even have enough tickets for your own kids. So, I mean, forget about old neighborhood friends that you have still in the area here. You're going to be a busy man. >> Yeah, I've got one of my sons uh really wants to go to Syracuse, so he'll be he'll be maybe close enough. He's got one more year before he makes that decision, but uh I just got caught up in the fever like everybody else. text: Welcome in to Bears Weekly, a Chicago Bears Network production. Bears Weekly is brought to you by Advocate Healthcare, Athletical Physical Therapy, CDW, Conniey's Pizza, and Menor Light. Well, it's a big week for NFL fans, particularly an overly excited fan base that supports the navy blue and orange of the Chicago Bears. The schedule released Thursday of this week and then it all becomes real that the 2026 season is upon us. Good evening everybody and welcome to Bears Weekly on a special edition here on a Monday night on ESPN 1000 of the Bears Radio Network with Super Bowl winning Bears guard Tom the former Bears quarterback Jim Miller. I'm Jeff Jonia. We discussed the schedule, the just completed rookie mini camp over the weekend, and we'll hear from Bears head coach Ben Johnson and his coordinators Dennis Allen and Press Taylor. Also coming up, a conversation with veteran wide receiver Khalif Raymond, Dan Burill, Jordan Dreup, Katie Fox, our producers, Kendra Smith. In studio tonight, the executive producer of the Bears Radio Network, Eric Arstski. Good evening, boys. Uh the Bears getting through their rookie mini camp. Uh, it was good to see it was in the in the Payton Center, but just to see the the fundamentals and techniques being taught just to get them initiated. But you could see the speed of these guys that it's a faster team just with the rookie class alone, fellas. Tom and Jim, I I know uh speed kills and that's what this team wants along with some violent players. >> Right. I I want to say one thing about the announcement of the schedule this week. One of the first things Ben said at the podium when he got hired was the players got to be comfortable being uncomfortable. So, I do think that's another thing that this team is going to have to see once the schedule is announced. How does that fit in? cuz we saw Ben kind of adjust the practice schedule last year according to times and making sure the players were fresh. So, I am excited to see that. And one thing about rookie camps, man, it's really funny because the rookies, they see the other rookies and they're kind of all coming in there the same. And so, the next time that they come to meetings and on the field and stuff, when the veterans are part of it, it kind it changes everything. But you do see a group of athletes that have impressed the coaches and the scouts, you know, kind of get a a very, you know, understanding of what you chose and how they are on their feet. So, it is an exciting time for those rookies to come in the building and kind of showcase their talent even though a lot of the veterans are not there. I think that, you know, it doesn't matter how they were acquired, you know, and and how the players show up on the Bears doorstep or any other team around the National Football League. And it's uh basically you got to learn a new way of of doing things, how the Bears want things done, how they want things ex executed. We're all looking for competition and and we Ryan and I alluded to that a couple weeks ago after the draft. But, uh, learning our way of life is first and foremost. >> You mentioned that the players, the rookies learning your way of life. How different is the situation they walk into this year because the standard is set right away. >> Yeah. Well, I mean, it's uh hard to compare it from last year to this year. Do you feel any pressure like do you do you have a chip on your shoulder wanting to prove that you belong here or is there any of that [clears throat] inside of you? Yeah, for sure. You mentioned, you know, you're kind of working on the technique. title: Big Red Rage - Cardinals Draft Deep Dive With Assistant GM Dave Sears | Arizona Cardinals 2026
text: We bring the draft room to us in the form of assistant general manager Dave Sears. Dave, we look forward to it every single year. How we doing? Hey, so do I, Paul. Uh, what is it like? I mean, is it sort of like a game day atmosphere? You know, the adrenaline flowing. What are the three days like? The exclusive company that you keep in an NFL war room? Yeah, I mean, it's not that exclusive. We let a lot of people in and out of there, but I guess you're not on that list. So, anyway, no, it's We're off and running. Here we go. Yeah. Uh, no, it's fun. It's just a lot of fun, you know, it's a lot of work that goes into it. Everybody's excited for it. It's good to see, you know, really the whole year of work for all the scouts and personnel people come to fruition and everybody's just excited to get going. I know money has said in the past, you don't fall in love with a player, but you want to be convicted. When you're on the clock, I mean, is it almost instantaneous? At that point, you know, all the work, the big board, you know where things are trending when it comes to your time on the clock. I mean, how quickly are you able just to make that decision? Well, I think you know before that, you know, and the guys there, you know, who you're going to take if a trade doesn't materialize or something like that. You may pause for a minute. Hey, let's give it some time. See if some calls come in here. We have an opportunity to possibly move back or something like that. There may be a few players still there that you feel good about at that pick. So, in that situation if a trade materialize, you go with it. Otherwise, you just take the player. All right, so give us your feelings on Jeremiah Love, number three overall. What stands out? >> Yeah, really exciting. Obviously, the explosive athletic ability of the kid. He's a home run threat in weight and a half, and I think he had 42 touchdowns. And of those 42 touchdowns, I think the average was 24 plus yards. So, he's a he's an explosive player, a big-time weapon. Well-rounded guy, bigger guy than some people think. I mean, he's 212 lb or something like that. He can run inside, run outside, obviously, and he's also really good pass protector. And that's the thing, he's also a durable player. I'm not sure he missed a game with injury. So, very few fumbles, one fumble in his career. So, there's a lot of things to like. I mean, He told us at the draft party he's never been hawked. He's never been caught from behind, right? State sprint champion >> Yep. in high school. He had a 98-yard touchdown, 94-yard touchdown. Obviously a premium player. When you hear people talk about how running back isn't a premium position, what would be your response to that? Well, I I think, you know, we can talk all day about that, but it's hard for me to see that you know, you just look at the recent history of the NFC and a couple years ago, the 9ers go to the Super Bowl. Who's their running back? Christian McCaffrey. Then the Eagles win the Super Bowl. Who's their running back? Saquon Barkley. And then uh the MVP of last year's Super Bowl is a running back who gets paid in free agency. What does that team go ahead and do? Takes a running back in the first round of the NFL draft. So, I'm not sure where that comes from, you know what I mean? Yeah, that's interesting. What What gives more laughs in a draft room or maybe in the personnel department? The mock drafts or the post-draft grades? I mean, right? I mean, how are you supposed The grades come out almost instantaneously. Do you guys I know you guys go through some mock drafts and the scenarios. Do you ever grade yourself as a We'll look back on our drafts usually um three to four years after the fact and that you know, once you can actually see, "Hey, did this pick work out? Where are Where are we at with this player?" Where, you know, you're always doing that as a scout reviewing your own guys years uh down the line of, "Hey, was I right on this guy? Was I wrong on this guy? Why?" But he's got to have some time to actually develop into a player and see whether it's successful or not and what the reasons are. There's really zero point in analyzing it a week after, right? You know, it's obviously for entertainment purposes. All right, Big Red Rage presented by Emergency Air Assistant GM Dave Sears is our guest. You mentioned the Super Bowl champions. I think one of the unsung heroes on that Seahawks team was Gabe Zable. Plug and play. Started all 17 games at left guard a year ago. Sort of solidified that offensive line. Tell us about Chase Basantus. And what are the odds that he has the ability to compete from day one to be a starter? Well, I mean, all these guys have to earn their right to be on the field for us, you know, that that's not no question. Nothing's given to a rookie. And so, I think Chase certainly's is to have the opportunity just like all the guys are going to have opportunity to get on the field, but Chase is a guy he's a he's a true junior. He's played there. He's started at games at right tackle as a freshman. He's played both guard spots. So it's not like he can only play left guard which he played last year. We really like the intangibles. The guy's a tough guy. He's a a good to very good athlete, you know. He's got Coach Fry recruited the kid out of high school. So there's some familiarity there. Just been a good player. So we're excited about him coming in here and competing. See where it goes from there, but You know Mike LaFleur told the media recently, you can tell when you watch film if someone loves the game. You know, Chase Bisontis has sort of like that something extra little nasty attitude, likes to finish, the physicality. That's definitely apparent on film. >> Yeah, that's what you're looking for in an alignment, you know. You you hear the term dirt bag a lot. I think there's some of that to Chase where a guy you can tell the guy just doesn't mind getting dirty, you know what I mean? Doesn't mind being grimy and and finishing a play. And if that means he's got to stick somebody's face in the dirt, so be it. All right. And we know an offensive lineman's best friend is a quarterback, right? Or maybe vice versa. Either way, it's Carson Beck, first pick of round three. Obviously generated a lot of buzz just the position he plays. Has a lot of experience not unlike a Bo Nix or a Tyler Shook. What do you think? What was most decisive or what stood out the most in making him your pick at top number 65 overall? >> Yeah, well Carson's Carson's been a prospect that, you know, we've seen a lot. He's played a lot of football. He's been around college football for a while. You know, he's got 40-plus starts or something, I think. He's a guy that I think he left Georgia as the all-time leading completion percentage holder there and then he went to Miami and his completion percentage was even higher. So the accuracy obviously stands out. The fact that he's played in a lot of big games for winning programs. He was a state champion high school. You know, he goes to the national championship game, I think three times, twice as a backup at Georgia and then leads Miami there. He's also won an SEC championship. So the guy's been around big-time football, played in a lot of big-time football games. So the maturity of the player, the size, obviously the accuracy. There's a lot of positives with Carson. >> Yeah, the only real negative I've seen in scout reports would be his performance under pressure. You know, he he he he wouldn't be the only quarterback, right, who struggles under pressure. But is that sort of is that something you want to figure out or see in person? Yeah, I mean I you know, that's a little bit subjective. I think you know, to what are are you talking about blitzes, pass rush something like that? Are you talking about the moment? I think Carson's played in a lot of big games and you don't get to play in a lot of big games if you don't perform under pressure. So, you know, the the NFL game everything speeds up and all rookies have to adjust to that for sure. I mean on the other hand, he's the Fiesta Bowl offensive MVP in the semi-final, right? Leads the game-winning drive and and a game-winning touchdown run at the very end. So, you go in the round four and you make Caleb Proctor the first FCS player drafted. Obviously, you like some of the traits. What did you see on film there? Yeah, well, Caleb's a very good athlete, you know, and that's one thing that kind of jumps off the tape. We saw that live down at the East-West game. So, Caleb's a guy, he's a two-sport We draft a bunch of these guys and there's a lot of two-sport success in high school some of these guys and Caleb's another guy like that. He was a really good high school baseball player as well. State champ there, too, I think. And then you see just like that kind of athleticism of just a natural athlete on the football field who maybe has to add some bulk and size, maybe has to hone his technique a little bit, but there's a lot of raw athleticism there. We think the guy can pass rush and we think he can grow into a pretty good run defender. So, we think he's a scheme fit and we're excited to work with him. When he spends his career at Southeastern Louisiana and he had plenty of offers to go FBS his final year, at least according to him. He wanted to stay with his guys who he was recruited with. Is that where scouts earn their money trying to project from one level to the not just to the big time and the power four, but into the NFL from FCS? Yeah, I mean, certainly that's a harder projection because of the comp he's going against, but we you did see him against um you know, some FBS schools the year before this past year you see him against LSU. Then you get to see him in an all-star game and win against those guys, and so there's enough evidence of him being able to do it that you can carry that projection over. But sure, yeah, that is it's harder obviously than if a guy's playing at Miami to see him going into the pros or something. Dave Sears, assistant GM of the Cardinals here in the Big Red Rage presented by Emergency Air. All right, round five, Reggie Begel, Texas Tech, a Senior Bowl riser based on on what I saw. What all stood out about his game? Well, Reggie is a guy that you know, he [clears throat] he came from Miami of Ohio, that's where he transferred from Texas Tech, and he was over 20 yards a catch there. So we he's had production, then he goes and he leads Texas Tech in receptions. So he's been consistent player, he's had special teams background. He's a guy we think is still developing, had a good week at the All-Star game, and then we had some exposure to him both at the combine, and then brought him in on a 30 visit, and the guy's got kind of an infectious personality, just loves football, loves to compete. >> Yep. And so he's a guy, you know, what the term riser kind of gets used by uh some of the mock drafts and stuff like that cuz they didn't know where he started in the first place, and they might have just heard of him, but I think Reggie's had a pretty consistent career, especially the last 2 years, and so we always kind of felt good about him in the range we took him. You know what's interesting and is you look at the fact he ran what, the 4 5 6 40, yet he he says one of his best skills is taking the top off, and then a lot of scouting reports say he's really quick after the catch. Is that one of those game speed versus workout speed type dilemmas? Yeah, sure. I mean, you know, we're more concerned about play speed, which you're getting off the tape than time speed. Obviously, you'd like both of them to correlate, but I don't think I don't think Reggie's a guy we're concerned with the speed, you know what I mean? That's not depending on whatever the role the coaches put him in, you know, Reggie's can you release I would say is more important than your top end time speed, and then you got to get open and catch the ball first of all, you know what I mean? So And then you get an inside linebacker out of Iowa who ran a 4 5 6 40, 40-in vertical, right? Carson Shire, 183rd overall. If nothing else, this guy appears to be a special teams assassin. Yeah, Cars- been a really good special teams player. They had a couple, you know, NFL guys, long time starters playing ahead of the guy. Took him a little time to get on the field. Iowa does a great job of developing their players. The entire time Kirk Ferentz has been there, they've been an awesome developmental program. And Carson's not a you know I talked about multiple sport athletes. Carson was a really good high school basketball player. The guy I think he scored over a thousand points in high school. He had a 45 point game. You know what I mean? There's cool highlight tapes of the guy so you can see the athletic ability. Just need time to get on the field. So the special teams while he's developing as a linebacker and then he finally gets his chance and he has a good year this year and so we're excited about him. And I know when you get into round seven you're looking for players, right, with that athletic ability and and just the ability to develop them. I mean when you get a guy who had 34 starts at tackle in the SEC in Jaden Williams out of Ole Miss and 6'4" 307. I mean it would seem like um he's a little more equipped than most seventh rounders to maybe come in and compete. Yeah, and you know Jaden, you know, a guy you know, we use the term swing tackle meaning he can play both sides. He's a guy I think combined starts on both sides of the line might have been one of the top guys in the draft. So uh it's not like you're taking a guy who's only played left tackle projecting him to be able to play left and right. We've seen evidence of him starting on both sides so we feel pretty good about that ability at least. And then Jaden's another guy really good high school basketball player so um you know, we just think there's athletic ability there to develop with him. Five of the seven picks on offense. Last year was six of seven picks on defense. Is there a rhyme or reason to that? No, not really. I think usually it's just the way the board falls to you. You know, it's and it's it's true of staying with your board. If the best pick for you happens to be an offensive player, you know, so be it. Happens to be a defensive player, so be it. As long as you've got your guys stacked right then you should just stay with your board. Has the whole transfer portal and the NIL money changed anything about teams trying to evaluate and draft players? Well, I I think um I don't I don't know if there's a specific answer to that, but I think the NIL world in terms of players being one of the big concerns used to be as I was coming up a long time ago was how are these players going to handle all this money? Well, now they already have some of them have a lot of money. So, you don't have to worry about that concern cuz you've seen that play out already. So, that's an interesting thing to me and I the last 5 years or so the average age of the draft pick is getting a little bit older. We were our draft class this year, I think was the sixth youngest and it was the youngest draft class since money's been here that we've had so far and it was younger than the the league average at this point. So, obviously that's a little bit of a change like post COVID with NIL guys maybe staying in school an extra year another year like that. So, the age of the draft picks has gotten a little bit older. That's maybe something, you know. You know, I was on with the serious NFL guys and they asked me a question, what are the biggest camp battles? People are already looking ahead, right? You got the mandatory mini camp then you have training camp. Are there a couple positions that, you know, are on your radar? I said edge opposite Josh Sweat and cornerback just cuz it's so loaded. Yeah, I think I think cornerback's going to be a fun one for the fans watch cuz I think we have a lot of guys capable of making the roster certainly. I could see why why it's age, but you know, for guys in my shoes I'm looking at every all 90, you know what I mean? So, we got to figure out where these guys go. Well, another attendance record set by the draft this time in Pittsburgh, right? >> cool. I don't know what's the hotter industry right now, the the NFL draft every year or AI. I mean, at this point it's it's I mean, you're in a good industry to be in. I I heard you hosted a pretty good draft party this year yourself also. It was. We just we fed off the crowd. I mean, no doubt. Dave, we appreciate it and look forward to whatever you're Thank you for the insight. >> you, man. There you go. Dave Sears, assistant GM on the Big Red Rage. We're back right after this presented by Emergency Air.

Uh same guy that I you know that I recognized from being back in Tennessee. A guy that's in full of energy coaching the entire team running back and forth from offense, defense, special teams. Uh, I I don't I don't see a difference whatsoever. >> Is his like hands-on coaching kind of the same as it was in Tennessee? Has it grown since he worked with him? Like, how is that? >> I mean, I wouldn't say that it's grown. I think he's just very consistent with his coaching style. Um, even today they're doing like some special teams punt drills and he's, you know, you can, he's the loudest voice on the field, you know what I mean? Just coaching the guys, making sure guys technique is good, but at the same time still praising them. They do very well. It's not like he's just, you know, mfing guys or nothing like that. Um, and then obviously as we get into our competition stuff at the end pushing sleds, he's out there front and center yelling and things like that. So, no, it's definitely the same guy that I recognize since Tennessee. >> Kevin, why'd you make the decision to to come to New England originally? And having made that decision, tell me, are you are you glad to be here? >> No, I'm I'm very excited to be here. Um, you know, obviously when things didn't work out going back to Chicago, uh, you know, obviously New England was always going to be, um, I kind of like a dream scenario, you know what I mean? Cuz obviously as you get a little bit older in this league, you want to be able to play for teams that are contenders, but also you want to be in the builders with familiar faces. So, um, you know, Braves, you know, we had kind of had a conversation once Ray started and I was very happy that we was able to get a deal done. I was able to come back and play for him. you were teammates with AJ Brown in Tennessee and there's a lot of buzz about him potentially getting traded here. Is that something like the two of you talked about? Like how would you feel about reuniting? >> No, honestly I try to stay out of that part of the business. Um because when you talk about, you know, contracts or players moving teams and things like that, um you I want to be as hands-off as possible. We train together in Tennessee, so it's not like I haven't Hey, AJ, what's you know what I mean? So, but no, we honestly haven't talked about it directly. Um, and I'm don't know what's the situation there. I hope it can work. I hope he can come here and play for us. But, uh, that remains to be seen. I'm just trying to get to know the guys that we have here, uh, from Rome to Pop and all these other guys that we have here. So, but if we're able to get AJ, obviously, he's incredible talent, somebody I play with. Uh, he's a true number one receiver in this league. So, uh, that'll be awesome to pair up with him again. >> What was it like to practice against him when you were in Tennessee? >> He's unstoppable. Uh, I mean, this is obviously AJ's very talented still, but you know, this is young AJ, a lot to prove. Um, couldn't be covered in one-on- ones. Um, I remember I think his rookie year, um, you know, when AJ first came, I think he might have had like a hammy or something like that. And he was getting himself back into shape and things like that, but I remember the first game that he really popped out was against the Falcons in Atlanta. He scored two touchdowns and I he caught like a slant and took it to the house. And at that point, I was like, "Yeah, he's going to be a dog. he's going to be a really good player and he basically just took off since then. >> Kevin, how how do number one receivers from your perspective change the way you play defense? Like what sort of impact do they have? >> I mean, I definitely dictates coverage, you know, in any anytime you're playing against team, you're game plan and um a number one receiver dictates coverage. You know, if you know him being in Philly, uh when you're game plan against those guys, you still have to make sure you have the safety over top of AJ, which obviously opens up things for a lot of other players. So just imagine the red of his age there any guy you know obviously Chicago Justin Jefferson you know you're not going to every coverage and every play starts with knowing where 18 is and then making sure you almost got uh somebody right there in front of his face and somebody over the top. So that obviously opens up things and you may see a guy stats may not be as as great as this it was early in his career, but you know dictating that coverage is a big thing uh with receiver ones cuz like you said if you have a really good receiver two or receiver three now you can win a lot of one-on-one. So having a guy like him or any other receiver one in this league uh dictating that coverage is big for how offense and a defense just game plans. >> You had a good relationship with Mike AJ had a good relationship with Mike. What is it about him that you know relates to players such as yourself? >> Well, I think for one, especially if you're a young player in this league and uh you come into this organization, uh a guy like Mike Varel who's number one who's played in his in his league for a long time, had success pro bowls, all pros, won Super Bowls. So, when a guy gets in front of the room, he commands the room and command attention. He's coaching his technique or telling you uh effort and finish and all the things he talks about. Um it's very easy to buy in because he's done it at a high level. You know, I think for any of us players, um you want to be coached by somebody that's going to connect with you as well on a personal level. Um because I think that's what coaching is about. When you are um trying to connect with people on that personable level, people want to know that you actually care about them. You want to get to know them. It's not just, hey, how you doing? You see somebody in the hallway, it's like he's actually want to, hey, how you doing? How's your family? This and that and that. And uh I think it's makes it very easy for you to want to be able to play for a guy like that. And I think that's one thing that Mike does well. Kevin, we related to Mike's question about a number one wide receiver, a guy AJ, a tight end who can come in, a move tight end >> like last year in Chicago. Um, what does that do? How does that impact team defensively? >> It's huge cuz I think, you know, the way you're seeing the league now, um, you're starting to see a lot more bigger tight end sets, 12 personnel with two tight ends or three tight ends out there. Uh, because it just creates mismatches, you know what I mean? like there's not a lot of linebackers that can cover tight ends, you know, and some some tight ends nowadays, it's hard for a safety to cover them. So, you know, you have your traditional inline blocking tight end that can catch a little bit, but then you're starting to have these other tight ends come to the league that are basically slot receivers, right? If it's Coast and Lovelin last year, I think the Browns had a really good tight end Fannon last year who caught a bunch of passes in college. I think that's the biggest difference you're seeing that now a lot of teams want to have two really good tight ends. Uh if you can have both of them blocked, that'll be great. But sometimes you have the blocker and then you have the receiving one. Uh so that just creates mismatches because now, you know, we all know this league is a one-on-one league, you know what I mean? You got a lot of good corners, a lot of good DBs, a lot of good receivers, but when you add the element of really good tight ends in the slot, um now you can put them anywhere, you know what I mean? So it just creates mitch matches. And I think that's what these offensive coordinators are trying to do, just find a way to create mitch matches and, you know, get favorable one-on- ones to their advantage. What have you seen from May up close? >> I mean, he's he's a obviously he's a talented player, but I just think the work ethic that you see him uh leading from the front. Um I think that's very impressive for a young guy to do and has the confidence to do that as well. Uh I'm excited to, you know, go along this journey with him as well. Um and obviously, you know, he's obviously he's going to his third year, but to see as he continue to progress as a player in this league, I mean, he was already MVP runner up. Uh so I expect him to just keep growing and getting better. When you talk about tight ends, how important is it as a safety room to have someone like Hunter Henry on that other side of the ball to they brought in Julian Hill, you know, how important is it to have guys like that um to go up against in practice? >> You know, it's going to be huge. Me and Hunter uh was actually in the same draft class. I think he was second and I was third round. Uh so it's number one, it's pretty cool to see him still playing at a high level. Um, but yeah, no, it's important to be able to just get those reps uh with each other. But at the same time, just picking each other's brains. Um, just try to see how he sees the games from his side of, you know, his point of view. And the same thing for me, I try to give him tips whenever I can. Uh, but like I said, he's always been a really good talented tight end, a guy who has really great hands, can work the middle of the field. Um, but I'm also excited to see the young rookie as well, see how they use him as well. Um, so like I said, every I think every team wants to have as many talented tight ends as possible. Speaking of Hunter, I think last year Mike made a comparison personalitywise between Hunter and yourself in terms of kind of having a relaxed nature on the field and being able to make plays almost easy. I I can't remember exact words you had. Do do you how would you describe like yourself from that standpoint? And >> I've seen that actually. I remember last year Stretch uh cuz like I have a good relationship with everybody on the staff. Stretch actually sent me that last year. It was kind of joking because I don't know if y'all know but Vay was always had to like these media rules and say we don't do comparisons and he made a comparison. So, he kind of sent it to me as a joke. Um, but no, it was pretty cool to see. Um, you know, I kind of just look at myself as, you know, I always try to be, when I first came to league, I was trying to be a leader by example. Uh, just working hard, just doing all the right things, but then eventually as you, as you get a little bit older, uh, you're kind of thrust into that leadership position by, you know, being vocal and things like that. Um, I guess just my position. I've always tried to be um, you know, I'm when I kind of look at myself like coming out of the draft like I may have not been the fastest safety. I may have not been the tallest or has the best ver or whatever may be. Um, but just my playmaking ability and also uh, being able to be cool and calm under pressure. Um, and I think a lot of that is just preparation and things I do every single day. uh the film study, taking care of my body and things like that allows me to go out there on game days and just play free and not play with like a you know a nervous energy or anything like that. Just always trying to be under control and also just trying to be example for everybody else in the building. >> Final questions. >> You were asked a lot about um Mike and how that impacted your decision to come here, but did Zack Core play a factor in that at all? You kind of talked about having spent some time. It was it looked like all sides were playing to him getting that DC job when he did. I'm very familiar with all the guys on the staff, whether it's him, Book, uh, Todd Downing, uh, Thomas Brown, I was with him in Chicago. I mean, it's countless guys. I mean, even Terrell's still here, so that's big. Um, the our administrator of player development, uh, Mitch, he's here. He was our team chapl in Tennessee. So, it's a lot of familiarity in this building for me. Uh, so I just think that was huge to be able to, you know, kind of be on the back side of my career, being with people that um knows what it takes to win, but at the same time, it's just familiar, you know what I mean? So, I just I just really enjoy that part of it. And that was a big thing for me coming here. Um, they didn't necessarily have to like recruit me or send out a recruiting pitch. Uh, obviously a team that's come off a Super Bowl, you want to be able to play for a team that, you know, has a winning culture, and that's that's what I'm all about. You you mentioned earlier talking about Craig, you want to help him get some turnovers this year. >> I think the number's 36 interceptions for you in your career. >> That is great. >> What is the key if you had to pinpoint one? What's the key to being able to get your hands on the football? >> Anticipation. Like you may get one or two a year where the ball is just thrown right to you. You just got to catch it. I think if you look around the league, a lot of DBs will have three or four picks just based on the ones that they don't drop. You know what I mean? Like, you know, if the schedule comes out, it'll be very clear for me to see just who our opponents are, just gaining an edge there. You know, just things of that nature. So, >> Romeo, you mentioned you're I paraphrasing here, you're a man of few words. What What have you noticed about being here in New England that's just a different feeling for you than anywhere else you've been? Uh, it's just Oh, that's a great question, man. I would say just that the hunger and energy in general. Like, I knew coming here it would be a test on my end prior to, you know, being a part of a team who was just in the Super Bowl. And it gives me an opportunity to understand, you know, that grind. Not to say that I don't have that, but just the process to that because I know everyone's goal, all organizations goals is to go to the Super Bowl and being a part of a team like this, you know, catching up is one thing.
