Tristan and Luke get raved about how much he helped them almost like a like a extra coach. Can you speak to him returning to your locker? Well, it's great having Justin back and uh just great having him in the MI room, having around. He's got a great personality. He's a great worker. He's a great professional and there's some good experience for guys to lean on certainly and he's just a smart, intuitive player that's uh been around at different places and certainly at our place. And I'm just excited to have him back. He's great in the me room. He's great on the practice field. And even that 2024 season when he stepped in and started uh at the Giants at left tackle, Philly at home uh at Atlanta, at Detroit, he played some big meaningful games for us there. >> Notre Dame's Billy Stra. It's kind of hard to evaluate lineman sounds about pads on this early, but um what are some of the things that you saw from him? Some things that you liked from his rookie mini camp. >> Yeah, just Billy from the rookie mini camp. you saw his uh at a young age coming in new, how serious he takes it, his mentality, his mindset, and the way he approaches the meeting room, the practice field, and just as you can see some of the movement skills and the physical traits that certainly we saw on tape at Notre Dame come to come to life. And uh yeah, bottom line is at this stage, you just want to see the guys mental intensity and uh the professional approach come in and develop and then pick it up as it goes along. What was your initial thoughts on Paul Rubelt, a incredibly large guy, >> 610? Yes, we had Paul in for the local workout for the local Florida kids and it was good to get to know Paul and then he's been he was good in rookie mini camp and uh for a young man that grew up in Germany and then moved to the states and then played at Central Florida and uh that's that's a lot for anybody to move across the ocean and go to college here and start playing football and I' I've appreciated where he's at in the game and we'll continue to develop and work with Paul and uh excited about him. Speaking of backup tackles, when you you know, it's really important to have a good swing tackle. I think you guys might have too with with Ben Chukuma and uh Justin School coming back, can you just talk about the development from from Chuck Wuma and how he was able to play so well in those spots where he had to start? >> Yeah, certainly proud of Chuke's growth throughout the from camp, excuse me, from the offseason through the camp and then through the course of the season. He continued to get better during the season as it went on and progressed and continued to develop and you know taking extra time on his own, taking extra time after practice and different settings. His attention in the meeting room and but for a guy that's played so little football before he came to the Bucks, what I've been impressed with was just his ability to retain and apply apply things and uh we'll continue to develop Chuke and he'll continue to get better and on his own and he'll continue to grow and I'm excited about his future. It's it's not easy anytime you lose both, you know, guards for the the season, both starting guards. Um, how much did that how much did health impact, you know, some of your your inside runs that maybe were a little bit more successful the previous year? >> Well, you know, anytime whoever the five guys are playing, you try to do what they do best. And so that's an evaluation you make every week during the season. And as the season goes on, you decide, hey, what we're doing well, what we're not doing well, and apply it going forward. Um, and so you really just try to find what these guys do best and go from there. >> What will it do for this offensive line to have Cody Mount back this season? >> Well, it'll be exciting to have Cody back. It has been exciting just having him on the grass and uh feeling his presence and his personality and uh just excited to have Cody back. It's it's an exciting time for him. you know, he played every snap in 2024, started every game in 23 as a rookie and played those first two games for us last year before he suffered that injury and uh just excited to see continue to see his growth and development in his fourth year. >> Kevin, it's not often you get to coach somebody or basically teach somebody a new position NFL level. Want to ask you just the first impressions of Nash and what what he showed you switching up to guard. >> Yeah, I mean, and you saw it a lot at uh when he was a defensive lineman. see the movement skills, you see the center of gravity uh that he can play with balance and high school wrestler in South Dakota before he went to Nebraska and some of those natural traits that you feel like can convert to guard. >> I know that you're focused so much on getting your guys ready, but obviously this team invested a first round draft pick and and Ruben Bane Jr. just from your perspective. Um, I know so much has been made about about the lack of arm length and things like that, but but what do you like about him and how much of a factor really is that as he's trying to get to the quarterback? >> Yeah, from just what I've seen from him in the brief period of time in rookie mini camp and then of course the highlights that you've seen and just blinking through his Miami tape is just just his explosiveness, how hard he plays and those are things that stuck out to me on tape and all the other factors didn't really seem like too much of an issue when you put the tape on and watch the guy. And then here at rookie mini camp, you can see the explosiveness, the suddenness, the athletic ability come to life. And then also too, how hard he plays. >> And how much how about like leverage wise, like how how does that kind of help him? I know um Jason Light was talking about kind of like he had a little more of a lower center of gravity, how that may help him. >> Sure. Um >> yeah, I think just in the history of the NFL, there have been some very special pass rushers with that aren't super long. Going back to Dwight Freeny for example or even Collijah here or Aaron Donald at the Rams. I know the last two guys I mentioned were interior players but certainly their explosiveness, the way they play and their style of play makes a difference but certainly you know guys like that create challenges for offensive linemen >> forcing some of those longer guys to bend. >> For sure. Absolutely. >> Is the last line your your backup center essentially or is that an open competition? Oh, well, all these guys are backup centers, and we expect these guys to do both. They have to because with the only dressing eight, you want you're you're going to have to have three guys that can snap on game day, you know. Um, and so we train these guys all to all snap, you know, and uh want to develop them in that regard. And so Dan has background, Dan Fine has background at center. Klein's been working at center in his last two years here. Bred's of course started those three games at center for us last year. And uh yeah, you really want to cross trainin all your inside guys. And so all those guys are getting work at the center and guard position. >> Anything else? All right, thank you. >> Awesome. Thanks. Good seeing you.

title: Skip Peete on Bucky Irving’s Determination | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: I don't know about all that. >> [snorts] >> How you guys doing? I'm going to put my water down. But Kenny Gainwell, just just what he brings to this running back room. Uh I think Kenny brings a lot of versatility. Um he has ability to be very competitive in the run game as well as the passing game. I think he showcased that in his years in Philly and as well as in Pittsburgh. Do I need to talk a louder? Obviously Bucky went through injuries last year, uh a lot of other things, you know, that uh they had to battle. How is he now uh you know, physically and mentally and and just having Kenny there, obviously you got Sean, too. How will How will those three guys kind of balance the load, so to speak, if they're all healthy? Right now, I mean, Bucky's on track to be ready to go and all of that. Um I think the combination of Kenny and Bucky are very similar as far as the skill set and their abilities to play size. Um they're both capable of I mean, obviously running the ball well as far as running routes, catching out of backfield. And obviously um they're not very large people, but they're willing pass protectors that's willing to do that. And if both showcased they can do that. I think Sean to this point has continued to improve. he flashes sometimes and does a good job, and I think he will continue to get better. Bucky uh was was open on social media and a little bit with us as far as, you know, just how difficult it was for him being away from football with the injury. He talked about getting baptized. He even mentioned that he had hit like a rock bottom. How have you seen him grow as a person during that time? Um well, sometimes guys have never been in those type of situations and then I mean, I think every person kind of handles those things a a bit differently, but I think um what I see in him right now is the the guy that I've always known. I mean, he's back to normal. He's back to being the guy that's working out every single day. He's um doing everything that that is expected of him as far as the training room and the strength staff has him doing. And I think he's um dialed in as far as he's in the meetings and everything like that. So, I mean, he's studying just like he always has. I think he's in a good place right now. I think he's going to be very um excited to get an opportunity to get out there and practice. He's particularly fond of you from everything I've heard. How has your relationship with him grown while he's undergone some of those trials and tribulations? I think with anybody, whether it's I mean, any player or any coach relationship, I mean, there's somewhat of a bond. I think you you kind of lean on each other. I mean, what do they need from you and then what is expected of them and then what is expected of me. And I think >> we have a good understanding of that. I mean, if there's a question or anything that needs to be answered or a situation that needs to be handled, we obviously discuss that. And I think I mean, it's no different than I do with my kids. So, I think it's you know, really these guys are like my kids. So, I mean, if there's a situation that arise, you talk it out and you try to make the best decisions you can for that situation and move on. As good as you look at last season, obviously you you guys want to try and get back to the run game you kind of had in '24, if you will. How much is a healthy offensive line, especially healthy interior offensive line, make that an easier process? Um I think every every year you want to have an exciting and explosive offense and sometimes you can't determine, you know, what position is going to be injured or what section of the offense may be injured, but I think um if you're hitting on all cylinders, I think it's an opportunity to have a very successful season, but I haven't been in a season where any position has always been completely healthy. So, I mean, we got to figure out >> how we can do whatever we got to do depending on no matter who's in there and continue the success that we've had in previous years. But I think we have the ability to do that with the guys we have. With Zach Robinson's offense, what he did in Atlanta, a lot of getting backs in space and things like that. How is this group of guys kind of able to fit some of that? God, this is going to should be pretty exciting. I think we have the guys that are capable of doing all the things that he would like to do in his offense from running the ball to catching the ball out of the backfield and um playing receiver. I mean, the things that they did with Bijan Robinson, they did with Algier. I think it's very similar to a lot of things we did um with Bucky and with Shaud back when he was here. So, I mean, very similar offense. Skippy, you mentioned that Sean Tucker's improved since coming in and kind of developing, but with the way that the room is right now with Bucky and Kenny, what's Sean's best role in contributing? Well, the way I always see the position is everybody's got to understand everything, you know, and obviously there's only one ball. So, I mean, you can't give it to everybody, but I think um last year was an example where I thought Sean had improved and he kind of became our short yardage goal line runner and obviously he had to split time sometimes on first, second down, which I mean, he's capable of doing so. Right now, I kind of see them all as first, second, and third down guys and then as the season approaches, then we have to kind of determine and decide on who's going to be in those exact roles. Kenny wasn't a a starter in Pittsburgh, but he was so incredibly valuable and you look at the production that he had. What what allowed him to be able to have that type of production despite the the label? Besides the label? No, I just think Kenny is a very exciting and intriguing player because of his ability to play on all three downs and his ability to understand route running from being the slot receiver in college. Um he's very similar to a guy coached in Pittsburgh, I mean in Dallas by the name of Tony Pollard. I mean they both played together. Um Tony was a slot then he became a running back. So I think he has a good feel of born being both in the backfield and in the slot or as the number one receiver outside wide. Um he can he can do it all as far as that's concerned. And I think Bucky's kind of in that same boat. Um we didn't necessarily utilize him like that because we always had Rashad that was kind of more that role. Skip you guys kind of swapped out your depth behind the top four. Um moving on from guys like Wright and Wiley who've been around the league for a little bit. What do you think about Kadarius Calloway? Just what you like about him and and and what he might bring. I mean like every young rookie seemed like he was a very excited and um eager young guy. Um kind of raw and kind of new to the position. I mean this guy just played start out his career I think as a corner and safety and then became a running back and um I think he's polished his skills as a runner. He's a I mean a guy that has a little bit more speed than probably Shawn. I mean he's he's fast. I mean he's probably second fastest back we have. But I mean it's it's always exciting to look at a young player have him come in and then have him have an opportunity to showcase what he can do and I think he did a good job during training camp and that's why we signed him. And then uh for another young player, Josh Williams, he flashed a little bit during last preseason. What did you like from him and just kind of what he offers? Josh is an interesting guy. I mean Josh is very smart. He's very um conscientious of everything. He's uh he analyzes everything. He has good answers when you ask questions. There's no uh indecision in what he saw. Um I think he's improved since he got here. Um I liked him coming out of LSU. I thought he was a very good talented back. Um spent time with the couple of backs that they had there, which they typically get always doing college cuz you you might lose them due to NIL and all that stuff. But, I thought he was a good all around back that was capable of playing on first, second, third down. Um, wasn't the um, home run hitter like a couple other guys were, but he was always very consistent in in critical situations and things of that nature. He was always called upon. Anything else? Good. Any senior stuff? Yeah, thanks very much. You're welcome.

title: Zac Robinson Talks 2026 Offensive Outlook | Press Conference Live Stream
text: We had an opportunity to kind of look at this rookie class and um you know know right now all the players going to be all pro and all that but how do you Let's start, you know, with wherever you want to jump in. How do you think these guys will help you early on in the year? >> Yeah, you know, any rookie that comes in, they they have a long way to go, clearly. And so, you know, they get got their college systems and there's so many new terminologies that you're trying to pump the brakes a little bit from an initial um expectation, I guess. And so, but when you watch these guys, you know, on tape from college, you could see clearly with with Ted, there was a lot of excitement, you know, early in the process, even, you know, like early February when we're starting to dive into these guys and you're like, "Hey, have you seen Ted Hurst from Georgia State?" And so, there was a lot of like, you know, across the building. BMAC, obviously, our scouting staff does an unbelievable job identifying some of those guys. So, you could see a great skill set. Obviously, he's a true kind of ex receiver and um you know, you're never going to replace a Mike Evans and so you're looking for th some of those skill sets that have similarities, but um he can run, he's got great hands, um he's an instinctual player. Um you know, but again, he's going to have a long way to go, but there's so many things to like about Ted and just being with him um throughout rookie mini camp. Really smart, really intentional. He did a great job handling all the information over over a short amount of time. So, a lot of things to be excited about him. Then Bill, you know, Billy, um, his tape speaks for itself at Notre Dame. He's played a lot of football. Um, that showed in rookie mini camp. It's like, man, this guy looks like a vet, uh, offensive lineman already. Again, long way to go in terms of just learning, catching up. But, um, excited about him. And then Bowerer was somebody that, um, you know, our our guys, personnel guys, kind of raised up in in um, you know, same time around February. and you start watching him and you see him his journey and knowing the quarterback position and obviously he's transitioned into that tight end role and you love the the tenacity he plays with. He plays with an edge. Um he can run, he has some athleticism and like I said, he's got some toughness, you know, at the line of scrimmage. So, he's still learning the position, but um but yeah, you were excited about all those guys and and again the Jason and his group did an unbelievable job just kind of identifying, hey, what are some of those things uh that we're looking for for guys that'll help us out? But um again, we've got a great group of vets that fortunately they're not forced into action, you know, as as early as you need to, but um they'll be competing and we'll see kind of where it goes throughout August and as we, you know, get to the season. >> The origins of your of your scheme um don't necessarily have that true X receiver, but we have seen it though kind of in in later iterations. Just where do you kind of stand on that, especially now that you have a guy like Hurst in the fold? >> Sure. Yeah, having a true X is a is a weapon as an offense. You know, knowing that if that guy is a real threat on the backside and you can dictate some certain coverages certain ways, like that is a absolute threat. And so, uh, the closest guy we kind of had in LA was Odell, you know, when we got Odell in that 21 season and he changed the math with the defense and there's one-on-one opportunities when they don't. So, um, yeah, having a true X is a luxury. We've been seen it both ways though where he didn't have a true X and really all three receivers can play all three spots which is also tough on a defense because guys can line up everywhere and that's where you see the flexibility of J-Mack and Mech and CG. Those guys can line up everywhere and there's really no true X, no true F, no two, no true Z, but you got a bunch of different versatility from a from a pretty cool skill group. So, um you know, you could go both ways with it, but if you got a true X, it's it's definitely a weapon. If you look at this offense in 2024 when Liam Comb was here, reached a lot of new heights in terms of top five rushing and top five scoring attack and all that. You're you're very good friends with with Liam and maybe to spend some time with him and have you been able to kind of learn some things from conversations with him about what happened in 2024 and the personnel that you're inheriting and and maybe how to get back to some of that product? >> Yeah, absolutely. Liam and I talk almost every single day. And you know, obviously we were in the division together. So those two years like I was like, we're not talking ball. And so we didn't get a chance to talk much X's and O's and their personnel. You know, I obviously was watching the tape and could see it from afar. But um but yeah, it's been natural dialogue just, you know, in terms of how he saw guys and um the run game took kind of a new level like you mentioned with some different variety that, you know, we were used to from our system in in LA. They had some gap schemes going that they kind of, you know, fell into as the season progressed and ended up being really successful. So, um, yeah, those natural dialogues that Liam and I have now that, you know, he's on the other side in the AFC and we can actually talk, you know, real football. We don't play him next year. So, u, that's been good. He's he's been super helpful just with, you know, even guys on the staff. And, I mean, it's an awesome staff working with some of the guys for the first time with BMAC and, uh, Peely and some of these guys. Like, it's been a cool collaboration and and, um, it's been it's been a lot of fun just to kind of get get to know everybody around the building and and kind of build this thing the right way. One of these new additions to the team uh as a veteran is Kenneth Gainwell. Just your thoughts on him and how he fits into the running back room and really the whole offense. >> Yeah, I think the first thing this sticks out with Kenny is he's just a true pro. I mean, you you can tell how intentional he is when he works. Um the tape was outstanding really from Philly when you watched him in Philly, limited opportunities and you saw last year just what he can do in an extended role. And so, um you were super excited that that that was able to get done and and he was able to be here. But just being around him, he's just a stud guy. Like a guy that you just want to be around. A guy that can ignite his teammates just by his style of play, the way he plays, and then uh the skill set is pretty cool. Obviously, you got Bucky who's got a unique skill set. Kenny and him kind of can match each other in certain ways with what they can do in the pass game. So, uh been awesome to get to know Kenny and and really the rest of the guys, but uh the biggest thing that sticks out is just how intentional he is and how great of a worker he is and just leads by example and and he's been awesome so far. been your impression about the vibe with Baker Mayfield this off season. You know that the team and himself didn't have the best year last year and then is banged up a lot, had a lot of injuries. This is level of of hunger and >> Yeah, I think that that word exactly like you can tell this group has an edge, you know, which you want to keep that edge, you know, things didn't go down the way that you had hoped last season obviously, but um that's why we're all here. And so I think that Baker naturally already has that edge to him. Um and you can feel it even more. He's been so intentional with his footwork and all the fundamentals and the details that that Whitmer and our coaches are preaching to him that he's he's off to a great start and obviously we got a long way to go with some things just learning some new things. There's there's a lot of carryover, but there's also a lot of new and he's diving into that. But um you definitely feel the edge and just the overall urgency from the group which is what you're looking for at this time of the year. >> We was one of the people you brought over here as a part of your staff. What was that process like? You know, bring some of your guys here and how has he been working with Mayfield? Yeah, Chandler's been great. I've known Chandler since he was in high school. I was an Elite 11 counselor as a college player and and I've I've known Chandler for forever. Obviously, we were able to get him on staff in Atlanta. He did a great job. Took an opportunity at Indiana. We were sick to lose him. And so, um you know, we had talked after that happened. I was like, man, the next chance we can get, you know, to get to work together again, we definitely want to um try to get that done. And he's been great. I mean, there's quarterbacks, quarterback coaches always love footwork. Chandler Whitmer takes that love to a whole another level. I'm pretty sure that's all he's thinking about at night when he goes home. So, he's been great. Uh just super, you know, fundamentally sound and detailed with his approach. And so, uh he'll be a huge asset for us, not only just coaching the quarterbacks, but scheme wise, helping out on third downs and and some of those things. So, Chandler's been great and he's he's just a great guy like the rest of the staff just to be around and to work with on a day-to-day basis. >> Zach, you mentioned like the wide receiver flexibility that you have with all the guys in the room. Well, how does that change your emphasis on ball distribution? There's maybe not a surefire number one wide receiver, but there's a lot of quality wide outs and it's a room that's very deep. >> Sure. It's a great question. I mean, I think it's a great problem to have. You know, like sometimes an offense can go through one guy or one or two guys. And uh the more that you can spread the football around and and get other guys involved and keep those guys on the other side of the football, you know, off a little bit, that's that's definitely a huge advantage. And so, uh, we have a ton of guys from a tight end standpoint, a receiver standpoint, a running back standpoint that can do a number of different things. And, uh, it's our job as coaches to make sure we're getting the we're dishing the ball around. And if there's a hot hand, we got to go to the hot hand, too. So, not losing sight of some of those things that naturally happen throughout a course of a game. But, um, no, it's a it's a fun group of guys to be around and just work with because, uh, the versatility of the whole entire group, receivers, tight ends, backs, is is pretty cool. when you need to score quickly though or or when you need like that that guy to to kind of make a play and like you mentioned that the guy that can even take the top off the defense. Um how how does Hurst potentially fill that that role? >> Yeah, absolutely. Again, we'll see where he can get to, but he has shown on tape that he can run by players. He can make contested catches down the field. Um like I mentioned, he's got great great ball skills down the field and he can track it. So, um all those things you mentioned and then body sizes. He's he's I'm playing DB routes on air and I just feel the speed and just how big he is when he's running at you. So that's um a huge asset to have. But um obviously if he can get to a point where hey we can package some stuff up for him um you know that would be outstanding. So we'll see kind of where he can progress to and and I definitely you know hope he can help us out. >> Zach, what's the next step for a Mecca or how how far can he go and what is it that he has to do from what was a pretty outstanding rookie year playing all four positions? But does he does he settle into one or you just like the idea that he can move around or? Yeah, we we'll settle him into one spot kind of our our Z spot and uh but again he in some instances he might look like he's playing the X, some instance he might be the F just based on the formation and how you can move him around. But Mech's um just getting to know him, you know, the last handful of weeks and and you guys have talked to him and and know him better than than I do at this point. But um it's incredible just I know I keep throwing the word intentional around, but that's that is him to a tea and and the amount of work and preparation um that he puts into it. He's very similar to like a Cooper Cup, you know, just in terms of the way that his brain works with the game of football and the natural instincts, but he doesn't have to change a thing. I think he's come back, he's refreshed, he played a ton of snaps, obviously played a lot of college football leading into that season and played a ton of snaps. So, um, you know, I think Mech's just going to take huge, huge strides. He's getting to know the new terminology and asking great questions. But, uh, Mech's just got to be Mech and do his thing and he'll be just fine. You guys have such a deep receiver room. But I wanted to ask you about Sills and what he brings and obviously having worked with you in Atlanta, how much that helps him as someone in the room that that knows the offense well. >> Yeah, Sils Sils is um he's a good player and he's been around for a long time. Hadn't got a ton of opportunities. Obviously got some opportunities last year. He was a guy that came in um last off season, you know, knew about him from his production at West Virginia and then um you know, he'd been kind of grinding on practice squads for so long that um you almost forgot about him, but he got there um incredibly smart player. Um he runs a lot better, you know, than than I think um anybody would anticipate. But uh very smart, very intentional, and he's been a great asset for like you mentioned some of these guys asking some of the questions with the new stuff. But um but yeah, we have great competition, you know, at the at the bottom of the roster with that receiver room and there's some good players obviously with Cam as well and um you know, there's a lot of depth to it, which you're excited about. Dennis Houston's looked great out there. So, we're excited for all those guys to compete, but definitely glad the Sills is here. >> 13 personnel coming and you ran a little bit 12 in Atlanta. You've seen Ber sharp at rookie mini camp, but uh what's your thoughts on the whole tight end room as a whole and kind of what you can do with them? Yeah, love the tight end packages that you can have with with both those guys. You know, Payne has been a guy that you throw on the tape and the physicality as a blocker and anytime it's been thrown to him, he's making plays as well. He hasn't had as many opportunities, but um see, you know, Kade and Payne, they've had some some great careers up to this point and and they'll just continue to progress. And then Bower is a guy that brings a unique skill set with some uh versatility. He lined up everywhere at LSU. He lined up in the back field. He was at tight end. He's out wide. They asked him to do a ton of different things. So, it's easy to see kind of a vision for how he could fit into that room. Again, he's got a long way to go from a mental standpoint catching up to those guys and seeing so many different snaps that Payne and Kate have seen. But, um, but yeah, you love 12 personnel. You know, I think the first year in Atlanta, we were the heaviest 11 personnel and then last year we were second most 12. And so, again, you're adjusting to who the best 11 are on the field. You love to get base defense out there to get some of those different looks um for the run and pass game. But um it's an exciting group with you add in coke Keef too who's a really good blocker. Um so there's there's some good versatility within that room and just looking forward to progress with Bower and the rest of those guys. >> When you look at your backfield in Atlanta, you had Bejan and then a big back and Tyler Rajir and the Bucks had that with Bucky and Rashad White. Your top three riding backs here are more similar sized in terms of closer to 200 pounds with Tucker and Gainwell and Bucky Irving. Do you like having kind of a similar type of backfield or would you rather have >> It's a really good question because you can go a number of different ways with that. You know, I think you can look at it from, hey, you got your bigger back like the Alers and then, you know, you look at the Rams and they basically have two guys that look identical. You can't even really tell which one's which unless you see the jersey number with Blake Corm and Kairen. So, can go a number of different ways. Personally, don't have like a preference one way or the other. our our you know personnel and Jason and those guys did a great job kind of identifying and and finding um you know Kenny and and understanding that hey it is a match skill set which that can be a good thing. You know there's there's not much you have to change when uh one backs out and one backs in. You can just kind of run your normal flow of your offense that you have for that game plan in that week. So um it's a good pro and then you know Tuck is you know he's a he is a little sturdier and he's kind of um been the short yardage guy and and Kenny's done some short yardage.
